finding: The sleep abstract reported no significant subjective-sleep or macrostructure difference, with reduced NREM alpha EEG. The shared-sample memory result was considered inconclusive.
limit: Sleep report abstract only; restricted acute sample. Memory analysis shares participants and uses exploratory analyses, so it is not independent replication.
scope: Acute Wi-Fi versus sham in healthy young men; subjective sleep, macrostructure and EEG.

finding: The waking abstract reported no measurable EEG-power or vigilance effect. The memory paper reported a declarative result its authors classified as inconclusive.
limit: Different endpoints and participant samples; abstract-only waking methods and exploratory memory analysis. No general cognitive effect follows.
scope: Acute waking EEG and vigilance, plus overnight memory in a separate project.

finding: Prospective cohorts did not show increased glioma risk under their studied conditions; INTERPHONE found elevated odds in its highest recalled-use group.
limit: Use proxies, recall and selection, latency and sparse extreme-use data limit causal conclusions. Selected reports, not a completed synthesis.
scope: Selected prospective cohorts and recalled-use case-control evidence.

finding: Selected cohorts did not show increased risk; the Swedish case-control paper found no conclusive overall association, with a highest-use signal.
limit: Multiple comparisons, few fully unexposed participants and mixed phone use complicate the case-control analyses.
scope: Mobile use and meningioma; selected cohort and case-control records.

finding: The report found no conclusive overall association; a highest cumulative-use signal lacked a consistent latency pattern.
limit: Retrospective exposure, multiple phone types and comparisons prevent one causal verdict for every cordless system.
scope: Recalled wireless-phone use in a Swedish case-control study.

finding: The pooled report described elevated odds with longer latency under its analyses.
limit: Small newer case groups, recalled use, mixed phone types and hearing-loss effects on preferred ear limit inference.
scope: Pooled Swedish case-control wireless-phone histories.

finding: The selected cohort did not show increased risk. Case-control reports differ, including long-latency or same-side signals with important uncertainty.
limit: Subtype rarity, recall, participation and hearing loss complicate comparisons. Studies overlap in exposure questions and should not be pooled casually.
scope: Cohort and separate case-control acoustic-neuroma diagnoses.

finding: The authors report a calling-time association, but group totals and reference-category interpretation require clarification. Numerical effects remain held.
limit: Printed case/control totals conflict with Methods; screen-time coding conflicts with generic prose. Self-report, selection and confounding further limit interpretation; no general other-cancer effect is established.
scope: A selected breast-cancer case-control report; different from brain-tumour studies.

finding: More frequent calls were associated with shorter gestation, while birthweight/growth findings did not show an association.
limit: Recalled phone use is a dose proxy; stress and other confounding may explain the gestation result.
scope: Phone-use histories across four birth cohorts.

finding: The report described a weak preterm-birth association and no birthweight association, interpreted cautiously by the authors.
limit: Incomplete follow-up, self-report, confounding and multiple analyses; pan, distance and wattage were not individual exposure measurements.
scope: Internet-based pregnancy follow-up using self-reported cooker use.

finding: The authors reported higher infertility odds for the closer distance category.
limit: Distance is a proxy; selection and confounding remain. Printed Table 2 has inconsistent counts, so numerical claims are held.
scope: Case-control residential distance to high-voltage lines.

finding: Average front-door measurements did not show an association; a maximum alley metric did under the authors’ analysis.
limit: Results depend on metric. No complete personal dosimetry or activity assessment; not a general causal finding for home wiring.
scope: Residential measurements and miscarriage in one cohort.

finding: The review reported an association in older blanket-use analyses, separately from measured residential fields.
limit: Small historical evidence base and study quality limit translation to a current product. No present-day product risk estimate is assigned.
scope: Historical electric-blanket-use studies within a systematic review.

finding: No clear consistent overall association; isolated time-window findings required cautious interpretation.
limit: Grouped exposure proxies, recall, selection and multiple comparisons; job title is not personal absorbed dose.
scope: INTEROCC job-exposure-matrix estimates; adult glioma and meningioma.

finding: No overall association or consistent exposure-response pattern; one intermediate category was elevated.
limit: Exposure misclassification and the isolated category result limit a causal interpretation.
scope: Job-matrix occupational ELF estimates and meningioma.

finding: No consistent acute skin-temperature response under the tested low-field conditions; pooled-analysis wording requires clarification.
limit: Pooled result labelled differently in prose and Table 1; interpretation held. Healthy adults and superficial short-term endpoints do not establish chronic safety or validate guideline thresholds.
scope: Controlled acute 26 GHz versus sham; superficial skin temperature.

finding: Call time was not associated with tinnitus or hearing loss in the report; a small headache result weakened with adjustment.
limit: Limited baseline call records, two symptom timepoints and self-report; no continuous personal RF dose.
scope: COSMOS symptom follow-up and call-time estimates.

finding: Tinnitus was more common in the sensitivity group, while phone-use measures did not explain the contrast.
limit: No measured field attribution; cross-sectional self-report cannot establish direction or an RF cause.
scope: Cross-sectional tinnitus and self-identified electromagnetic hypersensitivity.

finding: The linked sources characterize the specified exposure or assessment setting; they do not add an independent human disease trial.
limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Measured residential communication modules; transmission peaks, duty cycles and placement.

finding: The linked sources characterize the specified exposure or assessment setting; they do not add an independent human disease trial.
limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Parent and baby units of selected monitor systems, operating states and placement guidance.

limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Mouse and speakers during failed pairing; official Bluetooth context.

scope: Microwave cooking, US product standard, leakage, interlocks and heat injuries.

finding: The linked sources characterize the specified exposure or assessment setting; they do not add an independent human disease trial.
limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Defined pan, power, geometry and fixed-posture induction exposure model.

limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Transformer-related model in a DC charging system, rather than whole-vehicle exposure.

finding: The linked sources characterize the specified exposure or assessment setting; they do not add an independent human disease trial.
limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Mixed MRI components and task-dependent worker exposure; position-paper context.

finding: The linked sources characterize the specified exposure or assessment setting; they do not add an independent human disease trial.
limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Industrial equipment and task-specific worst-case RF measurements.

finding: The linked sources characterize the specified exposure or assessment setting; they do not add an independent human disease trial.
limit: Read the device, task, position, duration and source basis. A measured or modeled field cannot by itself establish a clinical risk or a treatment benefit.
scope: Complex workplace exposure and worker-specific assessment context.

finding: No consistent symptom pattern across cross-sectional, cohort and exposure-change analyses; isolated positive and inverse associations occurred.
limit: General cohort, not selected EHS cases; modelled dose proxy, limited participation, multiple tests and related HERMES reports constrain interpretation.
scope: Swiss adolescents; modelled fixed-transmitter ambient exposure and one-year questionnaire symptoms.

finding: Headache comparisons did not show a consistent exposure-related pattern.
limit: Observational ambient-exposure contrast; cannot reproduce an acute sham experiment or establish individual risk. Related HERMES family.
scope: Swiss adolescents; modelled base-station/broadcast exposure and questionnaire headache impact.

finding: Most outcomes showed no consistent adverse pattern; highest ordinary-call insomnia association weakened with network-based RF weighting.
limit: Observational proxy and questionnaire indicator; unmeasured behavior/stress, selection and multiple tests. Related COSMOS programme; exact report overlap unresolved.
scope: Swedish/Finnish adults; baseline operator voice-call/network metrics and later self-reported sleep.

finding: Isolated task differences occurred in mixed directions; evidence of a consistent association was limited.
limit: Parent-reported call proxy, low use, attrition, short follow-up and multiple comparisons; transformed scales and a printed table inconsistency. Related earlier ExPOSURE report.
scope: Australian primary-school ExPOSURE follow-up; reported changes in voice calls and repeated cognitive tests.

finding: Isolated task differences occurred in mixed directions; evidence of a consistent association was limited.
limit: Parent-reported call proxy, low use, attrition, short follow-up and multiple comparisons; transformed scales and a printed table inconsistency. Related earlier ExPOSURE report.
scope: Australian primary-school ExPOSURE follow-up; reported changes in voice calls and repeated cognitive tests.

finding: Authors reported higher listed model SAR in the small-for-gestational-age group; daily use-time was similar.
limit: No measured maternal/fetal dose or reported adjusted causal model. Education-table/test inconsistency unresolved; same-data cutoff is not a safety threshold.
scope: Selected Konya hospital deliveries; listed phone-model SAR and recalled daily phone use.

finding: No statistically significant actual-exposure effect on well-being in the reported questionnaire analyses.
limit: Short controlled exposure; no equivalence bound, individual symptom cause or chronic residential safety inference. Perceived exposure is a separate observational contrast.
scope: Acute blinded UMTS crossover in selected adults with and without self-reported RF sensitivity.

finding: Two nominal task/group findings did not survive the reported adjustment for multiple cognitive endpoints.
limit: Selected volunteers, practice and completion differences; no consistent impairment, clinical equivalence or transfer to chronic/current-generation exposure.
scope: Acute UMTS crossover; reaction, working-memory and attention tasks.

finding: No statistically significant tumour increase under the reported survival-adjusted analysis; exact counts and a zero-exposed-tumour claim remain held.
limit: Rare events, different survival/growth and apparatus exclusions; table/Results contradict Discussion about an exposed cardiac schwannoma. Coordinated Japan–Korea programme; no direct human risk estimate.
scope: Japanese male rats; prenatal-to-lifetime whole-body handset-type RF at one level, with sham and cage controls.

finding: Cellular bands contribute to onboard RF; a reading inside a bus is not automatically attributable to its motor or battery.
limit: Local vehicles/routes and dependent readings. Averaging, time labels and reference comparisons require clarification; exact numbers and compliance claims held. No health or implant outcomes.
scope: Band-selective RF measurements at sampled positions on operating electric buses in Samsun, Turkey.

finding: Some longitudinal contrasts were nominally significant without a consistent adverse exposure-response pattern across outcomes and exposure measures.
limit: No formal multiplicity correction; proxy exposure, selection, missing sleepiness item and replacement assumptions. Linked nested actigraphy is not independent replication or EEG architecture. No cordless-specific causal or Wi-Fi switch-off conclusion.
scope: QUALIFEX adult sleep follow-up; cordless/mobile call durations and separate ambient-exposure surrogates.

finding: Sleep-domain patterns differed across household indicators; these were exposure proxies, with no router-on/off intervention or objectively measured overnight Wi-Fi dose.
limit: Earlier device/use recall and current sleep in the same questionnaire; many comparisons, selection and printed estimator/count issues. Questionnaire scores are not lost minutes or diagnosed insomnia.
scope: ABCD children; reported home Wi-Fi/cordless presence, modelled ambient RF and parent-rated sleep.

finding: Mixed sleep-domain contrasts, including some more favorable cordless contrasts, do not form a consistent adverse pattern.
limit: Same children as the Wi-Fi row, not replication; household presence is not personal dose. Questionnaire chronology, multiple tests and printed labels remain under review.
scope: Same ABCD child sleep analysis; home cordless/Wi-Fi indicators and recalled calling.

finding: Authors reported adverse sperm and tissue/apoptosis-related changes; progressive motility and most organ weights were not significantly changed.
limit: Unquantified dose, traffic and temperature; incomplete sham/allocation/animal-unit description. Mixed duration pattern and unresolved printed labels/statistics; no mating or human fertility outcome.
scope: Male rats in an antenna/chamber setup described as Wi-Fi, with differing daily durations.

finding: The main matched analysis showed no clear association; alternative models gave weak elevations with wide uncertainty.
limit: Very sparse highly exposed cases, location proxy, country/model-specific samples and incomplete confounder reconciliation. Pilot exposure measurements are not study-child doses; Finnish reanalyses are not independent cohorts.
scope: TransExpo registry comparisons; apartment position relative to built-in transformer rooms.

finding: Authors reported shorter wrist-estimated sleep in the higher evening call-dose group; broadly null all-day findings after their correction procedure.
limit: Overlapping samples and different sleep instruments; estimated dose closely tracks calling, not isolated RF. Exact multiplicity/table details and clinical importance remain unresolved.
scope: Generation R/INMA preadolescents; modelled all-day dose and smaller repeated evening mobile/DECT call analysis.

finding: Authors reported worse subjective sleep and selected EEG differences, with most architecture, actigraphy and HRV comparisons not significant.
limit: Small pilot, retrospective registration, multiple tests and unresolved protocol/registry/clinical-threshold issues. Adult baby-monitor experiment, not infant evidence or a WLAN router trial.
scope: Healthy adults at home; multi-night active/sham FHSS/GFSK baby-monitor crossover.

finding: Most comparisons were not significant; selected task and exploratory gender contrasts lacked a consistent general pattern.
limit: Cross-sectional baseline and many unadjusted comparisons; parent-child reporting disagreement and printed tables need clarification. Same cohort family as R052 follow-up.
scope: ExPOSURE baseline child cognitive tasks and parent-reported mobile/cordless calling.

finding: No detected significant adverse count, morphology or tissue-weight pattern; more non-progressive movement at the higher field did not demonstrate fertility improvement.
limit: Delayed sampling, separate higher-field cohort and lost motility data; no mating or human fertility outcome. Laboratory coil results do not establish risk from using a cooker.
scope: Measured intermediate-frequency magnetic coil exposure in male mice; later sperm and tissue indicators, not cooking exposure.

finding: Adverse sperm biomarkers coexisted with no detected impairment in the selected IVF and early embryo comparisons.
limit: IVF selected better motile sperm; no natural mating, live birth or later offspring endpoint. Dose wording, animal counts and biological hierarchy unresolved; not a pocket-phone trial.
scope: Whole-body waveguide RF in mice; mature sperm, testis markers and selected laboratory fertilization/early embryos.

finding: Some early language/motor screens were more favourable among phone users; other adjusted screens showed no association.
limit: Historical behaviour proxy without fetal dose; correlated social traits, paternal comparisons and selective follow-up. Neither RF developmental benefit nor absence of every possible developmental effect established.
scope: MoBa maternal reported phone talking during pregnancy and parent-reported preschool development screens.

finding: Lower mean birth weight was reported, without a detected significant increase in the clinical low-weight category; a sparse transport association was imprecise.
limit: Near-delivery/birth reporting, social/mental-health confounding, sparse events and printed table/model differences. No fetal RF dose, radiation-specific causal effect or safe-use threshold.
scope: Local JECS-related pregnancy analysis using text-message dependency/excessive-use behaviour, ordinary users as reference.

finding: No clear association in harmonized data; expanded literature analysis reported a borderline paternal association with publication-bias concerns.
limit: Job averages and missing histories, expanded-analysis overlap and supplement/denominator issues. Parental occupation is not the child’s residential field dose.
scope: CLIC parental job-history ELF estimates around conception/pregnancy, harmonized childhood ALL/AML comparisons.

finding: No significant RF-related differences in the reported assays under the tested conditions.
limit: Specific altered cell models, challenges and short exposures; no powered equivalence or chronic intact-person conclusion. Supplement caption/reference issues remain under review.
scope: Characterized 3.5 GHz 5G chamber/sham exposure; established skin-cell redox and UV-lesion/repair assays.
